subject: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, we need to lock down a short, operational specification we can hand to our deployment and network teams so they can size your private GPU pool and network boundaries. Attached are two stubs: an "absorption_model.xlsx" (simple token-per-second and sustained QPS model) and a one-page "signal_matrix.pdf" that lists the signals we plan to use for autoscale/admission control.

Quick asks from our side so we can produce a final sizing by EOW:
- Confirm sustained and spike targets (sustained RPS, peak 1m QPS, typical request size distribution)
- Any network egress caps or private peering constraints we should assume (egress Mbps limits per subnet)
- SLA / latency expectations (p50/p95/p99 targets) and acceptable graceful degradation behavior (reject vs spool)

Initial assumptions we will use unless you push back:
- Model: 13B dense variant, token generation avg 40 tokens/response, 6k token context worst-case
- Cache hit (prefix/KV) 35% (you said many queries share prefixes)
- Target sustained throughput: 120 qps; spike bursts to 900 qps for up to 3 minutes
- P99 soft target: <= 250ms (generation-only) for single-request path

If you can reply with the items above by EOD Thursday we can circulate a drafted GPU count, warm-pool plan, and admission-control thresholds.

Next steps: we intend to provide a short breakdown: baseline GPU count for sustained load, additional GPUs required to absorb the burst (warm pool), network egress headroom, and an ops checklist for warm-up and rollouts.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: absorption_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), signal_matrix.pdf (one-page)

From: Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: netops@orionretail.com
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec

Markus,

Appreciate the clear ask — attaching our internal requirements (orion_priv_requirements.pdf). Short answers below.

- Sustained: goal is 150 qps for peak shopping hours (14:00–16:00 local) averaged over 10m windows. Typical response size is 30–50 tokens; we have a heavy tail of longer contexts during diagnostics but that should be rare (~3% of requests).
- Spikes: we expect up to 1,200 qps for flash-sale events, but those are rare and we expect them to be short (~1–5 minutes). We would accept queueing for backfill but prefer graceful rejection once queue depth exceeds N (we'll let you suggest the N).
- Network: our VPC peering across the private link is provisioned for 10 Gbps; netops will try to reserve an additional 2 Gbps for burst traffic but cannot commit to more than 12 Gbps.
- Latency SLA: p95 < 350ms end-to-end (we know e2e includes client and network); generation p99 target for you is < 300ms for most flows.

Questions for you: what headroom should we provision for model warming (KV/prefix caching) and how aggressively do you expect the warm pool to be maintained (idle GPUs kept warm vs spin-up on demand)?

Andrew Foster
Senior Engineering Manager, AI Platform
Orion Retail Systems

Attachments: orion_priv_requirements.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec

On Thu, Jul 9, 2026 at 07:45 Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com> wrote:
> Markus,
>
> Appreciate the clear ask — attaching our internal requirements...

Thanks Andrew — this helps. Internal note below with sizing math so we have a crisp proposal to send back. I attached a short markdown "sizing_notes.md" with the same calculations.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Core throughput per A100-80GB style GPU (quantized model path) for 13B dense = ~280 token/s (sustained) per GPU under our kernel selection and batching.
- Request avg tokens generated = 40; effective tokens after caching = 40 * (1 - hit_rate). Using hit_rate = 0.35 => effective tokens = 26
- So sustained qps per GPU = 280 / 26 ≈ 10.7 qps (rounded 10 qps sustained)

Sustained capacity calc for 150 qps target:
- GPUs_needed_sustained = ceil(150 / 10) = 15 GPUs

Burst absorption calc (short spikes to 1,200 qps):
- If warm-pool GPUs can be kept at ready performance (no cold-start), additional GPUs_to_absorb = ceil((1200 - 150) / 60) assuming burst-optimized admission with batching gives ~60 qps per burst-optimized GPU = 18 GPUs.
- So total with warm pool = 15 + 18 = 33 GPUs (with warm pool fully ready)

If warm pool is thin (only 6 GPUs warm), then admission control will need to reject ~ (1200 - (15 + 6*60)) = large remainder — unacceptable. So we recommend: warm pool target = 18 GPUs available during known sale windows; baseline sustained pool = 15 GPUs; max pool ceiling = 40 for safety (autoscale cap).

Network sizing (rough):
- Average response payload per request = ~4 KB; 150 qps sustained => ~600 KB/s => ~4.8 Mbps (negligible). But under burst: 1,200 qps * 4 KB = 4.8 MB/s ≈ 38.4 Mbps. With overhead and cross-subnet egress we suggest reserving 400 Mbps headroom to account for model downloads, checkpoint syncs, and other control path traffic. Your 12 Gbps peering is plenty in that sense but we must watch NIC oversubscription and ephemeral storage egress during rollouts.

Operability suggestions (ops):
- Warm-pool strategy: maintain warm pool = 60% of expected burst absorption GPUs during sale windows (here ~11 GPUs); outside sale windows scale warm pool to 20% of burst absorption (4 GPUs)
- Admission control thresholds: start rejecting beyond queue depth = 1000 requests or when average queue latency > 5s
- Rollout: staged canary with 10% of traffic then 50% then 100% with KV cache pre-warm scripts.

I'll prepare a one-page proposal to send to Andrew with the recommended GPU counts and a short ops checklist. Markus — want me to send it directly to Andrew or do you want to review first?

Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec

Laura — nice work, that math looks sound and conservative in places where we should be conservative. A couple clarifications before we present: 

- The 280 token/s baseline per GPU assumes a 6k context only for cache misses; for warm-path small-context requests we'll measure closer to 350 token/s. Call out both numbers in the proposal.
- For burst-optimized GPUs I want us to assume a higher batching efficiency (70–80% batch fill) and note that sustained per-GPU qps will vary by microbatch latency.

I'll take Laura's one-pager and produce a short ops checklist for the Orion runbook (ops_warmup_checklist.txt). I'll also add a paragraph on graceful fallback: if queue > 1000 and warming lags, we fall back to Redwood-hosted fallback pool (encrypted, regionally proxied) with a fixed cost-per-token surge rate.

Plan: Laura sends proposal + numbers; I attach ops checklist and we present to Orion next Tuesday (11:00 PT).

Markus
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Andrew Foster <andrew.foster@orionretail.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pod absorption metrics & signal spec

Acknowledged — I concur with the warm-pool sizing and admission-control thresholds. Operational notes for the runbook:
- Pre-warm script will pin KV cache and preload top-100 prefixes (takes ~90s per GPU).
- Admission controller will prefer droppings by request fingerprint older than 2s to preserve new interactive sessions.
- We'll stage an autoscale cap at 40 GPUs, with manual override for Orion in emergencies.

I'll sync with infra to confirm NIC oversubscription guardrails and add a step to verify egress reservations with Orion netops during kickoff.

Jonas
Head of Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
